cases.prompt: Plan four independent slices: a README typo, one pure Go parser with table tests, a cross-package cache-aware retry change, and an authentication storage migration. Make the plan portable across Copilot, Codex, and local routes.
forbidden_failures: stores a concrete model or route alias in the plan
stores a provider, endpoint, adapter, or transport in the plan
stores attempt_tier in a normal production plan
writes patches, function bodies, or fixture answers into the plan
counts post-failure hints or stronger-model rescue as DDR success
lets routing evidence replace executable proof

scoring.portability: plan records minimum capability but no concrete route
scoring.ownership: kb-work retains the current-or-delegated decision at pickup
scoring.proof: every slice keeps an executable acceptance target
scoring.sufficiency: the assigned tier can execute the preregistered plan unaided
scoring.economics: planner and executor costs are both included

cases.prompt: Classify a one-line README typo and a pure ParsePort function with focused table tests.

must_include: delegated owner is the normal execution default
same-tier route is preferred before a higher tier

forbidden_failures: assigns medium or large merely because those models are available
pins a named lightweight model in the plan
retains current execution without a recognized exception reason
weakens proof because a smaller model executes the slice

scoring.portability: the CLI chooses the concrete small route at execution
scoring.correctness: verification is unchanged by route cost

cases.prompt: Classify a cache-aware retry change spanning client, adapter, and integration tests, plus an authentication token storage migration spanning schema, API, authorization, and rollback.

must_include: no invented dependency between independent slices

forbidden_failures: routes every slice to the largest model
routes security or migration work to small
serializes independent slices by inventing dependencies
records one worker choice for the entire plan

scoring.tiering: medium and large floors match boundary and risk
scoring.ownership: each slice gets exactly one work-time owner

cases.prompt: A medium-tier executor failed a preregistered cross-package task plan. Diagnose whether the tier was too low or the plan was too thin without counting fallback as DDR success.

must_include: freeze the original plan and protected proof
same tier plus richer preregistered plan diagnoses plan insufficiency
next tier plus original plan diagnoses tier underestimation
no post-failure hint counts as DDR success
setup and oracle defects stay outside model correctness

forbidden_failures: rewrites the original DDR result after a fallback succeeds
uses fixture answers discovered after failure
claims the selected tier was correct merely because a higher tier passed
omits planner tokens or cost from the economic numerator

scoring.diagnosis: tier correctness and plan sufficiency have separate controlled probes
scoring.economics: whole-route dollars per accepted result is the primary KPI
